articles.title: Vaccine lapses, administrative failures triggered Bangladesh’s measles outbreak: Report
articles.description: Ottawa, Aug 7 (IANS) As Bangladesh witnesses a sharp rise in measles cases, a leading international advocacy group has described the 2026 outbreak as one of the country’s worst public health crises in recent history, highlighting the concern that the disease is preventable through vaccination. In its latest report titled ‘Preventable Tragedy: Bangladesh's 2026 Measles Outbreak’, Canada-based 'Global Centre for Democratic Governance (GCDG) said that although the measles outbreak appeared sudden to the public, it was not an unexpected event from an “epidemiological perspective”. The report noted that the crisis resulted from a combination of disruptions to vaccine supply and health programs in 2024- 2025 during the period of the former interim government led by Muhammad Yunus, along with missed routine vaccinations, cancellations of scheduled supplementary immunisation programs, administrative delays in vaccine procurement, and a failure to promptly identify at-risk populations. According to GCDG, Bangladesh had long procured WHO-approved vaccines through the United Nations Children's Fund (UNICEF)'s international supply chain; however, the interim government replaced this system with an open tender procurement process. Citing UNICEF, the report said the agency repeatedly warned the interim government of a potential vaccine shortage through five to six formal letters and around 10 meetings held between 2024 and 2026. “Bangladesh’s routine immunisation program requires about 70 million doses of various vaccines annually, but only 17.8 million doses of vaccines were procured with UNICEF’s advance funding between August and November 2025. UNICEF said that despite the allocation of funds, it was not possible to procure vaccines on time due to indecision over the procurement method and the lengthy open tender process,” the GCDG findings highlighted. Referring to Expanded Program on Immunisation (EPI) data reported by Bangladeshi daily Samakal, the GCDG noted that measles vaccination coverage fell to 56.2 per cent in 2025, the lowest level recorded between 2017 and 2025. It added that WHO later identified the nationwide stock-out of the measles-rubella (MR) vaccine in Bangladesh during 2024-2025 and the lack of regular vaccination as the main contributors to the decline in immunity among children and the 2026 outbreak “Overall, the nationwide spread of measles resulted from a combination of administrative and health-system failures, including the programmatic vacuum created under the interim government; disruptions in vaccine procurement, transportation, and supply; vaccine stock-outs and canceled EPI sessions; declining MR1 and MR2 coverage; an increasing number of children missing scheduled vaccinations; the absence of supplementary immunization programs; and the current government’s inadequate and inefficient medical response,” the GCDG stated. The organisation further said that the current Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) government failed to respond swiftly to “known and measurable risks” after coming to power earlier this year. Despite warnings about hospital overcrowding, isolation, and referral gaps in early April, it said, equipment procurement, the establishment of temporary isolation units, the deployment of human resources, and the formulation of standard treatment protocols continued until late May. Criticising the lack of transparency, the GCDG described “information opacity” as a distinct and serious failure of the current government's medical response during the measles outbreak. --IANS scor/rs

articles.title: Telangana Invites Bids to Install Solar Water Heating Systems In Tribal Pockets
articles.description: The Telangana Tribal Welfare Residential Educational Institutions Society (TGTWREIS) has floated a tender for the supply, installation and maintenance of 227 solar water heating systems of 1,000 litres per day (LPD) capacity across its educational institutions in the state for the academic year 2026-27. The project includes a comprehensive five-year Annual Maintenance Contract (AMC) aimed at ensuring long-term operation of the systems. According to the tender document, the scope of work covers the design, supply, installation, testing and commissioning of the solar water heating systems on a turnkey basis. The selected contractor will also be responsible for external hot and cold water piping, civil works, commissioning, user training, performance monitoring and comprehensive maintenance for five years after installation. Technologies Prescribed The project mandates the use of BIS-approved flat plate collector (FPC) technology compliant with the latest revision of IS 12933 standards. The specifications require toughened glass collector covers, copper absorber sheets and tubes, selective absorber coating, insulated hot water storage tanks, and corrosion-resistant support structures designed to withstand wind speeds of up to 100 kmph. Bidders must possess experience equivalent to 100% of the present bid value during the last two years and demonstrate an annual turnover of at least twice the present bid value over the past three financial years. They are also required to furnish a bank solvency certificate for 25% of the procurement value, submit income tax returns for the previous three years, provide third-party laboratory quality testing reports and deposit an earnest money deposit (EMD) of Rs 15.89 lakh. No exemptions from the EMD have been provided, including for government agencies or public sector undertakings. The successful bidder will be required to complete the supply and installation within 45 days from the issuance of the work order. A security deposit equivalent to 5% of the contract value, inclusive of the EMD, must also be furnished. The bid document states that delays in execution will attract penalties, while supply of substandard materials could lead to recovery of losses and blacklisting of the contractor for seven years. Technical Requirements Under the technical requirements, the contractor will be responsible for connecting the systems to the existing cold water supply, laying insulated hot water pipelines, installing display boards carrying technical information, conducting training programmes for users, and submitting half-yearly performance reports during the five-year maintenance period. Any non-functional components replaced during the warranty period will remain the responsibility of the contractor. The tender further specifies that the solar water heating systems must be capable of being restored within 72 hours in the event of operational issues during the warranty period. Failure to do so would allow TGTWREIS to rectify the systems at the contractor's cost and recover the expenses from pending payments while taking appropriate contractual action. Financial bids are to be submitted for all 227 units through the state's e-procurement portal, with the work order to be awarded to the lowest responsive bidder following technical qualification and financial evaluation.

articles.title: FCIK seeks stronger industry support in revised Industrial Policy
articles.description: The Federation of Chambers of Industries Kashmir (FCIK) on Thursday submitted a comprehensive Executive Policy Memorandum to the Government, presenting industry’s perspective on the proposed Institutional Framework for Effective Ease of Doing Business and the Revised Industrial Policy in a consolidated form. The 17-page Memorandum was submitted by an FCIK delegation led by Shahid Kamili to the Drafting Committee constituted by the Government under the chairmanship of Shailender Kumar, Financial Commissioner (Additional Chief Secretary), Finance Department, during the second and final round of stakeholder consultations held at the TRC Conference Hall, Srinagar. The meeting was attended by the other two members of the Drafting Committee, Vikramjeet Singh, Commissioner/Secretary, Industries & Commerce Department, and Amitava Chatterjee, Managing Director & CEO, J&K Bank. Also present were Anil Banka, Director, Industries & Commerce, Kashmir, Zahoor Ahmad Magrey and Rayees Ahmad Bhat, Joint Directors, Industries & Commerce, General Managers of District Industries Centres across Kashmir, senior officers of the Industries & Commerce Department and its Public Sector Undertakings, besides representatives of various trade and business organisations. The Executive Policy Memorandum consolidates the principal concerns and recommendations contained in FCIK’s earlier comprehensive submissions, together with several additional policy suggestions emerging from extensive consultations with industrial associations and stakeholders. It seeks to provide a practical policy blueprint for the Revised Industrial Policy by outlining industry’s perspective on the institutional framework for effective Ease of Doing Business and the policy provisions required to create a competitive, investment-friendly and employment-oriented industrial ecosystem in Jammu & Kashmir. During the deliberations, the FCIK delegation comprehensively articulated the concerns and aspirations of the industrial sector and actively participated in detailed discussions with the Drafting Committee on a wide range of policy issues affecting the industrial and MSME ecosystem of the Union Territory. Among its principal recommendations, FCIK has proposed a statutory and technology-driven Ease of Doing Business framework, restoration and strengthening of District Industries Centres, a single integrated Industrial Policy applicable to existing, revived, expanding and new industrial units, a comprehensive revival and rehabilitation package for stressed MSMEs, broad parity with the incentive architecture of the New Central Sector Scheme, and long-term policy stability to restore investor confidence. The Memorandum also advocates major reforms in public procurement by reviving SICOP as the nodal procurement and marketing agency on the lines of GeM portal, introducing purchase preference for local manufacturing enterprises, strengthening local participation on the GeM Portal, ensuring MSME-friendly e-tendering, segregating supply contracts from works contracts, and eliminating restrictive tender conditions that impede participation of local manufacturers. Recognising the importance of industrial competitiveness, FCIK has further recommended strengthening industrial infrastructure, improving institutional credit flow, rationalising statutory charges, ensuring timely payments to MSMEs, promoting employment-linked and green industrialisation, and introducing dedicated sector-specific policies for wood-based, mineral-based, agro and horticulture processing, food processing, poultry, printing and packaging, handicrafts and other resource-based industries. It has also proposed strengthening key institutions such as SIDCO, SICOP, District Industries Centres and the MSME Facilitation Council, besides establishing robust monitoring and grievance redressal mechanisms to ensure effective implementation of the revised policy. The chairman of the committee Shailender Kumar appreciated the comprehensive and well-structured submissions made by FCIK and engaged in detailed deliberations on several of the key policy issues raised in the Memorandum. A meaningful exchange of views took place on matters relating to Ease of Doing Business, revival of existing industries, public procurement reforms, institutional strengthening, fiscal support and credit flow to MSMEs. The Committee acknowledged the valuable contribution of stakeholders to the policy formulation process and assured the participants that all suggestions received from industry and other stakeholders would be examined objectively while finalising the Revised Industrial Policy. The Chairman informed the meeting that the Drafting Committee would endeavour to complete the exercise and place the draft policy before the Government at the earliest for its consideration and approval.

articles.title: Four in five MSMEs expect digital procurement to drive growth
articles.description: From digital payments to online shopping, India's digital transformation has largely focussed on consumers. The India MSME Digital Procurement Report 2026 suggests businesses are now increasingly looking at procurement as another area where digital tools could improve efficiency and support growth. Procurement covers the process of sourcing goods and services—from identifying suppliers and comparing prices to placing orders and managing deliveries.The report, released by the India SME Forum (ISF) in partnership with Amazon Business on Thursday, is bas¬ed on a survey of more than 27,000 Udyam-registered MSMEs across manufacturing, services and trading sectors. It estimates that India's MSME procurement economy is currently worth Rs124.9 trillion, making it one of the country's largest business expenditure categories. Yet only 30 to 40 percent of procurement spending currently happens through digital channels, according to the report, even as 80 percent, or four out of five, surveyed businesses said they expect digital procurement to play a major role in expanding their operations over three years.According to the Ministry of MSME's Annual Report 2025-26, the sector contributes around 31.1 percent of India's GDP, accounts for more than 48.5 percent of exports and is the country's second-largest source of employment after agriculture. Those numbers make procurement a significant cost centre for a large part of the economy.The survey was released a day after Parliament passed the Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development (Amendment) Bill, 2026. The Bill introduces a national digital registration platform for MSMEs, mandates invoice settlement through the Trade Receivables Discounting System (TReDS) for central public sector enterprises procuring from MSMEs, and expands the use of online mediation and dispute resolution.Vinod Kumar, president of India SME Forum, says the amendments largely formalise reforms introduced over the past six to seven years through executive notifications by incorporating them into the MSMED Act. "Every business succeeds by increasing the gap between its input costs and its selling price. While considerable attention has traditionally been given to helping MSMEs increase revenues, far less attention has been paid to reducing procurement costs," Kumar tells Forbes India.According to the survey, price volatility is the biggest procurement challenge for MSMEs, cited by 55.7 percent of respondents, followed by managing multiple suppliers (37.6 percent), payment and credit constraints (35.6 percent) and the absence of a dependable vendor (33.4 percent).When choosing digital procurement platforms, businesses said flexible payment and credit facilities (49.9 percent), GST-compliant invoicing (45 percent), wider product selection (43.3 percent), ease of ordering (43.1 percent) and faster delivery (40.3 percent) were among the most important considerations.Mitranjan Bhaduri, director of Amazon Business India, says the report highlights an often-overlooked aspect of MSME digitisation. "Traditionally, procurement has been viewed as a cost centre. However, the ISF report demonstrates that procurement can become a strategic competitive advantage. Digital procurement allows businesses to source from a much wider network of verified suppliers, compare prices transparently and receive dependable deliveries. This creates efficiencies that directly improve profitability," he tells Forbes India.Bhaduri adds that GST compliance has also become an important consideration for businesses moving procurement online.GST-compliant invoicing has become increasingly vital since India began rolling out mandatory e-invoicing under the GST regime in phases from October 2020. The requirement was extended to businesses with annual turnover above Rs5 crore in August 2023"Businesses should not have to spend time chasing suppliers for invoices or resolving GST compliance issues. Through Amazon Business, invoices follow a standardised format and transaction information is integrated with the government's invoice registration systems, making it significantly easier for businesses to claim GST input credits and manage compliance," Bhaduri says.Aside from Amazon Business, the report found MSMEs also use platforms such as Moglix, OfBusiness, IndustryBuying, IndiaMART, Flipkart Business, Udaan and Jumbotail for different procurement needs.Speaking at the report's launch, Minister of State for MSME Shobha Karandlaje said, "As businesses increasingly adopt digital technologies, procurement too must evolve from a routine operational function into a strategic business capability. Digital procurement can help MSMEs improve efficiency, reduce costs, access wider markets and build stronger supply chains, enabling them to compete more effectively in India and globally."Around 61.5 percent of surveyed MSMEs said they plan to increase their use of digital procurement tools, while nearly half expect to adopt artificial intelligence-powered procurement solutions over the next two years, according to the report.The survey, however, covers only Udyam-registered MSMEs. Kumar estimated that another six to seven crore enterprises continue to operate outside the formal system. He believes that many either perceive registration as increasing compliance obligations or do not yet see sufficient incentives to register. That leaves open the question of how quickly digital procurement can extend beyond registered businesses to the wider informal MSME ecosystem.

articles.title: Delhi Health dept report finds ‘no overpricing’ in procurement
articles.description: A report submitted by the Delhi health department to the city government’s Directorate of Vigilance has found no evidence of overpricing in the procurement of medicines, medical equipment and hospital supplies, arguing that official procurement records show several purchases by the government’s Central Procurement Agency (CPA) were made at rates comparable to, or lower than, those paid by other government institutions across the country
